notes: Active ownership is determined only by a successfully created exclusive-scope lock.
Claiming does not change task status.

Warden findings must include reproduction steps/evidence, severity, player impact and the recommended owner agent. Check the existing queue before creating a new task.
Small PR policy: one claimed task/scope per PR; avoid unrelated refactors. Split broad work into follow-up tasks instead of creating giant integration PRs.
Subjective quality policy: agents may report evidence about clarity, pacing, repetition and friction, but Josh is the creative director and final judge of fun/premium feel.
All black-box Warden QA must drive a real browser (Playwright, agent-browser or equivalent). Reading source/DOM alone is not a playtest.

Agent 7 — The Director owns design governance, not specialist implementation. It reviews work against docs/VISION.md, docs/DECISIONS.md and canonical terminology, flags cross-task conflicts, and proposes queue/dependency corrections.
Josh remains final creative director. The Director may protect and interpret established pillars but must not materially change product direction without Josh's approval.
Before a specialist feature PR is treated as merge-ready, The Director should perform a design-coherence review and record any blocking conflict or terminology/tone issue in the PR or queue.
Narrative authoring may proceed ahead of runtime/save integration when it is isolated to story/docs assets. Blocking engine integration must not unnecessarily idle the Storyteller.

Agent 1 follow-on engineering tasks should remain mostly blocked behind the relevant foundations; LR-0059 is the intentionally independent current lane so Steward work can continue without colliding with parked feature branches.

Josh's 4 Oct playtest direction: the player should exist in-world as party leader; active adventuring composition is leader + three companions; companions should have bounded personality-driven agency; dialogue should remember prior conversations/choices; action repeatability must be explicit; and the phone core loop should not require whole-page scroll shuttling between map and outcome.

BG3 is a reference for player-avatar-centred companion approval/dialogue and legible action-resource costs. Inkle's Sorcery! is a structural reference for remembered narrative state and map-centric cross-platform/mobile presentation. Adapt principles only; do not clone copyrighted dialogue, UI art or D&D rules.

agent_roster.name: The Steward

agent_roster.role: Narrative, characters, dialogue, quests, consequences, campaign structure and endings.

agent_roster.name: The Mechanist
agent_roster.role: Combat, equipment, abilities, injuries, builds, economy, balance and deeper gameplay systems.

agent_roster.name: The Lamplighter
agent_roster.role: Art direction, UI feedback, animation, map presentation, sound, ambience and overall feel.

agent_roster.name: The Wayfinder
agent_roster.role: Mobile UX, accessibility, save/autosave usability, touch/map behaviour, testing, edge cases and interaction audits.

agent_roster.name: The Warden
agent_roster.role: QA, black-box playtesting and player experience. Repeatedly plays Lantern Road, tries to break it, identifies bugs, exploits, confusion, tedium, pacing and fun problems, and routes reproducible findings back to the appropriate specialist rather than implementing feature fixes.

agent_roster.role: Design direction and production governance. Owns the product vision, terminology and decision log; reviews feature work for pillar alignment, tone/coherence, scope drift and cross-task conflicts; does not replace Josh as final creative director.

agent_roster.name: AED (Agent Efficiency Department)
agent_roster.role: Cross-agent efficiency, tooling, repository hygiene, coordination throughput, blocker/dependency analysis, code/process quality audits and systemic workflow improvements. Audits Agents 1–7 without taking over their active specialist work or product authority.
